section: Sultanate literature and culture - Amir Khusrau, Ziauddin Barani, Ibn Battuta, music and Sufi influence

accepted.s: Abdur Razzaq, who visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Deva Raya II, was an envoy from which region?
accepted.x: Abdur Razzaq was a Persian envoy associated with the court of Shah Rukh. He visited Calicut and Vijayanagara during the reign of Deva Raya II.
accepted.tq: Use the traveller–mission relationship to distinguish closely associated foreign visitors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following foreign travellers described diamonds being sold in heaps at Vijayanagara?
accepted.x: Abdur Razzaq described the sale of diamonds in heaps during his visit to Vijayanagara under Deva Raya II.
accepted.tq: Identify the traveller from a distinctive observation recorded in the travel account.

accepted.s: Afanasy Nikitin, a horse merchant who visited India during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II, belonged to which country?
accepted.x: Afanasy Nikitin was a Russian traveller from Tver, situated on the Volga. He visited Vijayanagara during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II.
accepted.tq: Test the traveller’s nationality through the associated ruler and occupation.

accepted.s: Tver, situated on the Volga, was associated with which traveller who visited Vijayanagara as a horse merchant?
accepted.x: Afanasy Nikitin was a horse merchant from Tver in Russia, located on the Volga. He visited India during the reign of Virupaksha Raya II.
accepted.tq: Separate the Russian traveller from the Persian, Afghan and Ottoman visitors by using the place-name clue.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Abdur Razzaq — Russia; Virupaksha Raya II’s time
Seydi Ali Reis — Ottoman Turkey; Humayun’s time
Afanasy Nikitin — Persia; Deva Raya II’s time
Mahmud Wali Balkhi — Morocco; Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s time
accepted.x: Seydi Ali Reis was an Ottoman Turkish traveller associated with Humayun’s period. The other pairs interchange the identities, origins or periods of different travellers.
accepted.tq: Check both parts of each pair—origin and historical context—before selecting the match.

accepted.s: Ibn Battuta was appointed qazi of Delhi and was later sent as an envoy to China during the reign of:
accepted.x: Ibn Battuta came to India during Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s reign, was appointed qazi of Delhi and was later sent as an envoy to China.
accepted.tq: Infer the ruler from the traveller’s office and diplomatic assignment.

accepted.s: Mahmud Wali Balkhi travelled in India mainly during which period?
accepted.x: Mahmud Wali Balkhi was a 17th-century visitor who travelled in the 1620s. He lived as a kind of sanyasi for a period.
accepted.tq: Use the century and decade distinction to eliminate historically close distractors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Mahmud Wali Balkhi is correct?
o: He was a Moroccan qazi at Muhammad bin Tughlaq’s court.
He was a Persian envoy to Vijayanagara in 1443.
He belonged to Balkh and lived for some time as a kind of sanyasi.
He was a Venetian visitor to the Kakatiya kingdom.
accepted.x: Mahmud Wali Balkhi belonged to Balkh in Afghanistan and travelled in the 1620s. He is noted for having lived as a kind of sanyasi for some time.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that combines the correct origin with the distinctive biographical detail.

accepted.s: Abdur Razzaq visited Vijayanagara in which year, according to the recorded account?
accepted.x: Abdur Razzaq visited Calicut and Vijayanagara under Deva Raya II in 1443. The year 1323 is associated with the fall of Warangal described by Firishta.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise visit year from nearby medieval dates associated with other events.

accepted.s: Which work of Isami describes the victories of the Tughlaq army over Warangal?
accepted.x: Isami wrote Futuh-us-Salatin, which describes the Tughlaq army’s victories and campaigns against Warangal. Isami wrote under Bahmani patronage.
accepted.tq: Match the campaign described with the correct chronicle rather than the chronicle’s patronage.

accepted.s: The work Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi was written by:
accepted.x: Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi, associated with the Sayyid period. The other authors wrote different Sultanate chronicles.
accepted.tq: Use the historical period as a supporting clue while matching the author and chronicle.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir, dealing with the reign of Aibak. Futuh-us-Salatin was written by Isami, Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi by Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi, and Mahmud Gawan wrote Riyaz-ul-Insha.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure author–work pair and reject the swapped chronicle names.

accepted.s: Riyaz-ul-Insha, a collection of letters, is associated with:
accepted.x: Riyaz-ul-Insha is a collection of letters associated with Mahmud Gawan of the Bahmani kingdom.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a collection of letters from historical chronicles and literary works.

accepted.s: Which of the following works is a treatise on political theory written by Ziauddin Barani?
accepted.x: Ziauddin Barani wrote Fatawa-i-Jahandari, a work dealing with political theory. Tughluqnama was written by Amir Khusrau, Taj-ul-Maasir by Hasan Nizami and Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi by Ferishta.
accepted.tq: Use the subject of the work—political theory—to distinguish it from narrative chronicles.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ziauddin Barani’s writings deal with Khalji-Tughlaq history.
2. Barani’s works contain attacks on south Indian kingdoms.
3. Fatawa-i-Jahandari is associated with political theory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Barani wrote on Khalji-Tughlaq history, criticised south Indian kingdoms and authored the political-theory work Fatawa-i-Jahandari.
accepted.tq: Test the author through three related dimensions: historical coverage, political interpretation and subject matter.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi — Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi
accepted.x: Hasan Nizami wrote Taj-ul-Maasir, not Futuh-us-Salatin. Futuh-us-Salatin was written by Isami, while both Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote works titled Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.
accepted.tq: Look for the swapped author–work pair, especially where two chronicles have similar titles.

accepted.s: The work Tarikh-i-Ferishta is also known as:
accepted.x: Tarikh-i-Ferishta is also known as Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi. It was written by Muhammad Qasim Ferishta of Bijapur.
accepted.tq: Distinguish alternate titles of the same chronicle from titles belonging to other authors.

accepted.s: Muhammad Qasim Ferishta, the author of Tarikh-i-Ferishta, was associated with which court?
accepted.x: Muhammad Qasim Ferishta was associated with Bijapur and the court of Ibrahim Adil Shah. Tarikh-i-Ferishta is also called Gulshan-i-Ibrahimi.
accepted.tq: Identify the author through the regional court with which he was associated.

accepted.s: Muhammad Qasim Ferishta was born at Astarabad in:
accepted.x: Muhammad Qasim Ferishta was born at Astarabad in 1552. He later became associated with the Bijapur court.
accepted.tq: Test a biographical year against nearby medieval and early-modern dates.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Ferishta’s account is correct?
o: It calls Telangana ‘Tilang’ and describes the fall of Warangal in 1323.
It calls Vijayanagara ‘Motupalli’ and describes its fall in 1443.
It calls Bengal ‘Tilang’ and describes its conquest in 1552.
It calls Delhi ‘Tilang’ and describes the rise of the Bahmani kingdom in 1620.
accepted.x: Ferishta refers to Telangana as ‘Tilang’ and describes the fall of Warangal in 1323. The other options substitute incorrect places, events or dates.
accepted.tq: Verify the place-name and event together; a single altered detail makes a long statement false.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the chronicles titled Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is correct?
o: The title was used exclusively by Amir Khusrau.
Only Ziauddin Barani used this title.
The title is associated with both Ziauddin Barani and Shams Siraj Afif.
The title belongs to Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi alone.
accepted.x: Both Ziauddin Barani and Shams Siraj Afif wrote works titled Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi. Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi wrote Tarikh-i-Mubarak Shahi.
accepted.tq: Watch for the ‘only’ trap when two authors share an identical or similar title.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Ibn Battuta’s Rihla is correct?
o: It is a Persian political treatise on Bahmani administration.
It is an Arabic travelogue dealing with the Delhi Sultanate and the Deccan.
It is a Sanskrit account of the Kakatiya kingdom.
It is a Turkish chronicle of Humayun’s reign.
accepted.x: Ibn Battuta’s Rihla is an Arabic travelogue containing observations on the Delhi Sultanate and the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Identify the work by combining its language, genre and geographical coverage.
